Whoa, whoa, whoa, we can't just let that slide without a story.

I've always had trouble sleeping. As a kid I'd wake up screaming from night terrors, and talk about the spiders on the walls and how the dolls would try to get me if I slept alone. I couldn't sleep by myself until I was in high school, or no one could sleep because I'd wake them up with the terrors anyway. In high school I just didn't sleep, staying up on the internet til all late hours, and I'd sleep in class ( teachers never minded because of my grades). I managed.

Anyway, I graduate, move out, get night jobs and do fine until I move in with a then - boyfriend and his really superstitious pagan girlfriend (they were polyamorous and I really needed a place to stay). I start having to sleep at night again and lo and behold the night terrors rear their ugly head. Everyone was desperate for sleep and so one day the superstitious girlfriend suggests bringing her professor friend over who does exorcisms, cause she thinks that I'm probably being haunted by something.

He comes over. Everyone takes their top off, except me, and he does his ritual. It involved water in bowls, oil, waving herbs - the whole shebang. He claimed that I did not have any major demons haunting my soul, but just a small "oily" one that liked to attack by depressing people and lowering their self-esteem. He gave me a rune necklace to help ward off any more demons.

For context, I was raised superstitious catholic (my grandmother would cleanse the "evil eye" off of me by rubbing eggs on my head when I was young and watching the cracked egg yolks in a glass of water) and eventually became atheist, though that superstitious bit is hard to shake off as a learned behavior. Although at the time I was non-religious, I agreed to it because I cared about not hurting the girlfriend's feelings and also pure desperation.

Did it work? Not really, I broke up with them and left a few weeks after that. Sometimes I wear the rune necklace around people who give off bad vibes.

Also, I sleep fine now, even though I still have night terrors a few times a year.
Wow, great story! Thanks for sharing. What eventually helped you sleep?

It was a combination of things - I figured out one day I was ridiculously anxious about a lot of things that I just needed to sit down and face.

I also fixed my diet(no more sugary things before bed!), and try to exercise regularly.

The real turning point was buying myself a brand new memory foam mattress though.

I felt really dumb after sleeping a whole week with no interruptions - I was just uncomfortable this whole time and I was losing my mind because I'm cheap about mattresses?

Sometimes it's a simple fix we've just got to find. I used to have regular panic attacks, ophthalmic migraines where I'd lose significant vision, and intrusive thoughts. I bounced around doctors who offered a combination of nothing and dangerous medication until going to a walk-in about the migraines and being recommended to try magnesium citrate. ("More easy for the body to absorb than magnesium oxide. My wife uses it.") Everything else cleared up along with the migraines. I guess I had some sort of imbalance that was costing me magnesium.
